stories.title: 81,000 warning letters sent to crypto holders in HMRC tax crackdown
stories.summary: HMRC sent 81,172 warning letters, emails and text messages to cryptocurrency investors in 2025-26 it suspects may have underpaid tax — a 25% rise on the previous year. Investors could face fines or prosecution if they fail to declare profits from selling or exchanging crypto, with new powers due next year expected to sharpen enforcement further.

stories.title: September 2026: future customs infrastructure arrangements at Sevington and Holyhead inland border facilities
stories.summary: HMRC published its September 2026 newsletter on future customs infrastructure arrangements at Sevington and Holyhead inland border facilities, providing updated guidance for traders on upcoming changes to customs checks closer to the border.

stories.title: Statement of Changes to Immigration Rules (HC 584) published 3 September 2026
stories.summary: The Home Office published a new Statement of Changes to the Immigration Rules on 3 September 2026, introducing amendments across a wide range of visa and immigration categories. The changes were presented to Parliament by Jo White MP, Minister for Migration and Citizenship.

stories.title: PM Burnham and Macron agree to scale up action on small boat crossings
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham met French President Emmanuel Macron to discuss small boat crossings, defence and Ukraine. The Home Office noted that 16,513 people have crossed the Channel by small boat in 2026 to date, with July recording the lowest monthly total since 2020 — attributed to UK-France collaboration and tougher enforcement including jailing of 10 small boat pilots.

stories.title: Home Secretary issues oral statement on small boat crossings
stories.summary: The Home Secretary issued an oral statement to Parliament on 1 September 2026 providing the latest government position on small boat crossings, outlining progress made and forthcoming enforcement measures.

stories.title: UK delivers statement at UN General Assembly on Russia's actions in Ukraine
stories.summary: The FCDO delivered a statement at the UN General Assembly on 1 September 2026, reaffirming that Russia's actions do not change Ukraine's sovereignty or rewrite its borders. The UK reiterated its full support for Ukraine's territorial integrity under international law.

stories.title: UK-France bilateral talks: Ukraine, small boats and EU cooperation
stories.summary: During PM Burnham's bilateral with President Macron, both leaders discussed the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, as well as defence cooperation and strengthening the UK-EU relationship. The meeting underscored the diplomatic importance of UK-France ties for Channel security and wider European stability.

stories.title: DWP completes migration of all legacy benefits to Universal Credit
stories.summary: The Department for Work and Pensions confirmed it has completed the managed migration of all legacy benefit claimants to Universal Credit — a major milestone after several years. Around 24 million people now claim DWP-administered benefits, representing approximately one in three people in the UK.

stories.title: September 2026 benefit and pension payment dates confirmed
stories.summary: DWP confirmed September 2026 payment dates for Universal Credit, Pension Credit, Attendance Allowance and other benefits, noting no bank holidays affect payment schedules this month. New benefit rates for 2026/27 took effect in April, including a 4.8% increase to the State Pension.

stories.title: SFI26 Window 1 closes; Window 2 expected to open 22 September
stories.summary: The Sustainable Farming Incentive 2026 (SFI26) Window 1 closed on 29 August 2026. DEFRA confirmed that Window 2 is expected to open on 22 September, open to all farmers and land managers in England. SFI26 includes 71 actions (down from 102 in SFI24) and now requires a minimum of 3 hectares.

stories.title: Defra statistics release calendar updated — 4 September 2026
stories.summary: DEFRA published an update to its statistics release calendar on 4 September 2026, covering annual and monthly releases across farming, environment, food and rural affairs data series.

stories.title: UK and Ukraine sign landmark AI defence partnership — Avengers AI Labs access secured
stories.summary: Prime Ministers Burnham and President Zelenskyy signed an AI defence partnership making the UK the first international partner to access Ukraine's Avengers AI Labs. The deal includes collaboration on fibre-optic AI sensors for military facility protection and low-power AI chips for drones, as part of the UK-Ukraine 100 Year Partnership.

stories.title: Defence Secretary champions innovation on visit to Devonport Naval Base
stories.summary: The Defence Secretary visited Devonport Naval Base — the largest Navy base in Western Europe — to see the latest equipment used by the Royal Marines and UK Commando Force. The visit highlighted innovation priorities in the UK's defence modernisation agenda.

agencies.name: BIST
agencies.description: Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (merged DBT + DSIT from July 2026)

stories.title: BIST publishes Algorithmic Transparency Record — 3 September 2026
stories.summary: The newly merged Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade published an Algorithmic Transparency Record on 3 September 2026, continuing the previous DSIT commitment to transparency around government use of algorithms and AI systems in public services.

stories.title: AI for Science Strategy published — UK targets frontier AI across industry
stories.summary: BIST published an AI for Science Strategy identifying AI as one of six frontier technologies central to the modern industrial strategy. The strategy targets five priority industries, with the Digital and Technologies sector plan framing AI as essential to driving economic growth.

stories.title: UK Tech Minister returns from G7 with signed deal on modernising public services
stories.summary: UK Tech Minister Ian Murray returned from the G7 Summit with a newly signed international agreement on modernising public services using technology, strengthening UK tech ties and positioning BIST as a key driver of digital government reform.

stories.title: Health Bill 2026-27 reaches report stage in Parliament — 7 September 2026
stories.summary: The NHS Modernisation (Health) Bill reaches its report stage in the House of Commons today (7 September 2026), marking a significant milestone in the largest NHS reorganisation in over a decade. The Bill aims to join up health information and abolish NHS England as a separate body.
stories.source: House of Commons Library / UK Parliament

stories.title: NHS kicks off flu jabs for children and pregnant women ahead of winter
stories.summary: NHS England launched its 2026 winter flu vaccination programme on 1 September, targeting children and pregnant women ahead of the winter season. The early rollout reflects lessons from previous years and aims to reduce hospitalisations during peak winter pressure.

stories.title: NHS Medium Term Planning Framework 2026/27–2028/29 published
stories.summary: NHS England published its Medium Term Planning Framework covering 2026/27 to 2028/29, setting out how NHS organisations should plan and deliver services over the next three years. The framework aims to drive coordinated change across the health system ahead of the NHS Modernisation Bill reforms.

stories.title: Royal Mail staff say they were instructed to hide post to disguise missed delivery targets
stories.summary: Postal workers from across the UK told the BBC they were asked to move or hide mail from senior managers to make delivery targets appear met. Royal Mail bosses are due to answer questions from MPs on Tuesday about ongoing postal delays affecting millions of people across the country.

stories.title: MPs accuse Royal Mail of 'lying' and prioritising parcels over letters
stories.summary: MPs have accused Royal Mail of 'lying' about its performance data and 'pretending' not to prioritise parcel deliveries over letters. The accusations come amid a parliamentary inquiry into persistent delivery delays, with Ofcom having previously fined Royal Mail for missing delivery targets.
